title: Noru audit pack manifest (.noru/audit-pack.yml)
description: What an auditor asks for, for one framework over one window: the controls in scope with what is expected of each and what is actually linked, the local artifacts that fill the gaps, a reproducible sample where a population had to be tested, and a workpaper per control saying what was inspected and what was concluded. This is the one piece that mostly consumes: the pack itself is a local deliverable, and what lands in Noru is the tested conclusion per control, which is the part that belongs in a register rather than in a folder. Enforced by plugins/audit-pack/scripts/validate_manifest.py.

queue_snapshot.description: The scope of the pack as Noru returned it: the framework, its controls, what the framework expects of each, what is already linked and whether a testing procedure is available. Written from MCP output by the client; never invented by this plugin. Requirement 9.

inputs.description: The local half of the pack, digested. Artifacts are the files an auditor asks for that never reach a server-side integration; manifests are the other pieces' committed records, named here so the pack says which reviewed inputs produced what is in Noru.

interpretation.description: Contract requirement 8. Who concluded this, when, until when, and why. `expires_at` is required and is measured from the END of the audit window: a workpaper concludes about a period, and signing it late does not extend what it covers.

pack.description: What this pack is: which framework, which period, and who assembled it. The window is the frame every conclusion in the file is about.

key.description: Stable identity for this pack. A new window is a new pack: last year's package is not this year's.

reviewed_by.description: The second pair of eyes. Optional in the schema and warned about by the validator: a pack nobody reviewed is a pack with one person's judgement in it.

control_id.description: The canonical lowercase internal control id returned as `id` by getOrganizationControls. `controlId` is the uppercase display form; store the canonical one.

testing_guidance_available.description: Whether getControlContext returned a testing procedure for this control. The procedure text is deliberately not stored: it is the API's to serve, not ours to vendor, and a pack that copied it would go stale the moment the framework moved.

upstreamManifest.description: Another piece's committed manifest, named and digested. This is what makes the pack an account of how the register was reached rather than a snapshot of what it happens to say.

inspected.description: One thing that was actually opened while testing this control. Not a list of everything that exists — a list of what somebody looked at.

reference.description: A repository-relative path for an artifact or a manifest; an evidence id from the queue snapshot for evidence.

sha256.description: Required for an artifact or a manifest: what an auditor gets handed has to be the bytes that were tested.

population.description: The set a sample was drawn from. Its digest is what makes the sample checkable: change the export and the conclusion no longer covers it.

sample.description: A sample anybody can redraw. The method, the seed and the size are all recorded, so an auditor with the population file can reproduce exactly this selection rather than taking it on trust.

seed.description: Required for deterministic_hash: the value the ordering was derived from. The collector uses the population's own digest, so the same file always draws the same sample.

drawn.description: The items selected, by a reference that finds the row again in the population.

key.description: Stable identity for this workpaper inside its pack.

control_id.description: The control this workpaper is about. One workpaper, one control: a single account mapped to forty controls is the antipattern that makes evidence useless to read.

evidence_item_ids.description: The framework-level expectations this workpaper satisfies, where it satisfies specific ones. Must be expectations the queue snapshot says the control has.

scope.description: What was tested, in the tester's own words. Not the framework's procedure — that is Noru's to serve.

conclusion.description: effective = it worked over the window. deficient = it did not. not_tested = nobody tested it, which is a legitimate answer and a much better one than a conclusion nobody drew.
